issue_context.title: outerVolumeSpecName should not set as innerVolumeSpecName when reconstructing volume
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:
Pods using ephemeral volumes stuck in "Error" status after node reboot.
```
dataplatform         40m         Warning   FailedMount               pod/dataplatform-catalog-platform-2tph8-d5c68b69b-ppdb5                                                                           Unable to attach or mount volumes: unmounted volumes=[log], unattached volumes=[default-token-nlnkv log]: timed out waiting for the condition
```
This pod uses an ephemeral volume outer-named "log", which is sourced from a storage plugin developed by my team. According to design, ephemeral volume's inner and outer name are defferent, for example:

volumes in pod spec:
```
  volumes:
  - name: log            <- outerVolumeSpecName
    tosdisk:
      accessMode: ReadWriteOnce
      capability: 20Gi
      name: log
      storageType: silver
```
While in `/var/lib/kubelet/pods/<pod_uid>/volumes/<pluginname>`, the inner volumename is defined as `<pod_uid>_<outer_name>`
```
[root@tos-126-11 ~]# cd /var/lib/kubelet/pods/a22dcd6c-9dfb-404b-9c37-cd78e963dfee/volumes/transwarp.io~tosdisk/
[root@tos-126-11 transwarp.io~tosdisk]# ll
total 0
drwxr-xr-x 3 root root 28 5月  27 17:37 a22dcd6c-9dfb-404b-9c37-cd78e963dfee_log
```
After system reboot, kubelet volume manager scans `/var/lib/kubelet/pods/<uid>/volumes/<pluginname>` directory to reconstruct volumes then cache them in asw and dsw. `WaitForAttachAndMount` function checks if all volumes in pod have been attached and mounted already by invoking  `verifyVolumesMountedFunc` periodically until timeout.
```
// verifyVolumesMountedFunc returns a method that returns true when all expected
// volumes are mounted.
func (vm *volumeManager) verifyVolumesMountedFunc(podName types.UniquePodName, expectedVolumes []string) wait.ConditionFunc {
	return func() (done bool, err error) {
		if errs := vm.desiredStateOfWorld.PopPodErrors(podName); len(errs) > 0 {
			return true, errors.New(strings.Join(errs, "; "))
		}
		return len(vm.getUnmountedVolumes(podName, expectedVolumes)) == 0, nil
	}
}

// getUnmountedVolumes fetches the current list of mounted volumes from
// the actual state of the world, and uses it to process the list of
// expectedVolumes. It returns a list of unmounted volumes.
// The list also includes volume that may be mounted in uncertain state.
func (vm *volumeManager) getUnmountedVolumes(podName types.UniquePodName, expectedVolumes []string) []string {
	mountedVolumes := sets.NewString()
	for _, mountedVolume := range vm.actualStateOfWorld.GetMountedVolumesForPod(podName) {
		mountedVolumes.Insert(mountedVolume.OuterVolumeSpecName)
	}
	return filterUnmountedVolumes(mountedVolumes, expectedVolumes)
}

```
As we can see, expected volumes are outer-named while mounted volumes are inner-named, that's why the ephemral volume will never been seen as mounted since the difference between inner and outer volume name, even though it's already been mounted in actual world.

This issue should be found for in-tree storage plugins with different ephemeral inner and outer volume name.


#### What you expected to happen:
Pods are "Running" after system reboot
#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):
reboot kubernetes node
#### Anything else we need to know?:
N/A
#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.16.1
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): CentOS 7.6
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): 3.10.0-693.el7.x86_64

review_comments:
I think outerVolumeSpecName is basically not possible to reconstruct. It is a name defined in pod spec, iirc.
So volumeSpec.Name() will not return the correct one either. 
We are not using this outerVolumeSpecName actually, I think.
